cognate: ON fé = Ved. paśu- = Av. pasu = Umbr. pequo < *péḱu
drift_or_renewal: *wiHro- 'man' renewed in ON by maðr (*mon-); ON fé has drifted toward 'property, money' but here (as in 'drepr bæði menn ok fé') still covers livestock
shared_syntax: coordinated pair 'men and cattle' as a merism for the whole living wealth of a community (ON 'bæði at mǫnnum ok at fé'; Ved. compound pair paśu-vid vīra-vid; Av. pasu vīra dvandva; Umbr. ueiro pequo)
context: ON: Óláfr ravages districts 'both of men and of cattle'; AV/Av./Umbr.: the pair is what the god or sacrifice secures or keeps unharmed (Umbrian prayer to protect ueiro pequo, Av. Yima's men and cattle undying). Same merism, inverse polarity (ravaging vs protecting), which is the expected pairing in war and prayer language.
note: Merism of men and livestock is the known Indo-Iranian/Italic formula (Watkins, Benveniste); ON keeps only the *péḱu member and the pair is a living saga idiom (~285 fé+maðr co-occurrences within 2 words in Menota), so inheritance through ON cannot be separated from natural pastoral language. Prose legendary saga, 13th c.

search_lead.argument: ON 'tekr sveininn í kné sér' (the king sets the boy on his knee and questions him about his future) ~ Gk placing/sitting a child on the knees (Od. 19.401 the newborn Odysseus set on Autolycus' knees to be named; Il. 9.455 curse that no son sit on Amyntor's knees): setting a child on the knees as an act of acknowledgment/fosterage (cf. ON knésetja). The slab's Hittite partner (KUB 36.89, Tešimi sleeping on the beloved's genuwa) and Il. 22.388 are not this motif; I could not find the Hittite Ullikummi child-on-knees scene in the index. Gesture may be universal.
